data.hook: A tanker crew spotted multiple explosions close by in tense waters off Yemen, but stayed safe with no harm or spills reported.
data.name: Explosions Reported Near Tanker South of Yemen's Al Mukha
data.summary: The UKMTO issued alert 151-26 on Sunday after the tanker's security officer reported blasts about 60 nautical miles south of Al Mukha, near the vital Bab al-Mandab strait. The crew emerged unharmed, no environmental damage occurred, and no responsibility has been assigned as investigations continue. Authorities urged nearby vessels to proceed cautiously and report suspicious activity, amid a pattern of recent tanker incidents in the area.

data.hook: In Yemen's second-largest city, Taiz, families face a full Houthi siege with roads blocked and supplies gone, while Saudi forces gear up for a major push nearby.
data.name: Houthi Siege Tightens on Yemen's Taiz as Saudi Offensive Looms
data.summary: Houthi fighters have seized all roads into Taiz and appeared on the route to Aden, raising fears of the city's imminent fall. Saudi Arabia plans a large offensive with over 100,000 Yemeni troops to retake the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, backed by airstrikes, as Pakistan sends 30,000-40,000 troops to defend against Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh and Aramco sites. The U.S. offers intelligence but skips combat, amid clashes that endanger key Red Sea shipping lanes.

data.name: Saudi Ambassador to Yemen Mohammed Al Jaber Announces Bab al-Mandab Strait Cleared of Houthi Militia
data.summary: Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to Yemen, Mohammed Al Jaber, stated that the Bab al-Mandab Strait has been cleared of Houthi militia remnants following the capture of Mayun Island by Yemeni government-aligned forces during Operation Dawn of Yemen. Saudi jets provided air support to these forces, including the Giants Brigades, in pushing back Houthi positions along the strait connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Houthi spokespersons rejected the claims, asserting they repelled advances and maintain control.

data.hook: Armored vehicles chased Houthi fighters along the sandy coastline near the vital Bab al-Mandeb Strait, reclaiming control in a rapid dawn offensive.
data.name: Saudi-Backed Forces Seize Key Yemeni Coastal Areas from Houthis
data.summary: Yemeni government forces, supported by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes, launched Operation Dawn of Yemen on Monday and captured Dhubab district, its airport, and routes to Mocha, severing Houthi supply lines. The Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a major global shipping route between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, saw intense clashes with videos showing pursuits by armored vehicles. Houthis responded by warning airlines to avoid Saudi airspace, claiming strikes on a Saudi Aramco refinery, and encircling parts of Taiz, while both sides accuse each other of misconduct amid unverified reports of war crimes.

data.hook: Wheelchair-bound sailors leaned on officials and family at Addis Ababa airport, finally heading home after months of captivity and loss.
data.name: Injured Pakistani Sailors and Fallen Crew Return Home from Somali Pirate Hijacking
data.summary: Four injured Pakistani crew members from the hijacked oil tanker MT Honour 25, along with the remains of three killed by Somali pirates, flew from Addis Ababa to Karachi on Ethiopian Airlines flight ET 694. Pakistan’s ambassadors to Ethiopia and Djibouti saw them off, following Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s directive for their safe return. The Palau-flagged vessel was seized on April 21 off Puntland with 17 crew aboard; Puntland forces recovered it on September 29 after pirates killed five, including three Pakistanis. Three uninjured Pakistanis remain on the ship as it heads to port, with critics like former minister Fawad Chaudhry calling the handling a state failure.

data.hook: An LNG tanker faced a tense encounter 140 nautical miles off Yemen's coast when a small boat with seven people fired shots and closed in.
data.name: LNG Tanker Fires Warning Shots at Approaching Skiff off Yemen
data.summary: On October 17 at around 1030 UTC, the tanker's master reported the skiff approaching near Al Mukalla. The boat fired two shots, prompting the tanker's armed security team to fire two warning shots in response; the skiff then retreated with no reported injuries or damage. UK Maritime Trade Operations urged vessels in the area to transit with caution, report suspicious activity, and stay vigilant amid ongoing investigations and other regional incidents. This adds to recent maritime alerts, including three more flagged that morning.

data.hook: In Yemen's tangled war, a new investigation claims the UAE has quietly helped the Houthis target Saudi-backed troops, raising questions about shifting Gulf alliances.
data.name: Report Alleges Secret UAE Aid to Yemen's Houthis Against Saudi Forces
data.summary: Drop Site News reporters Ryan Grim and Iona Craig cite four sources alleging UAE-aligned forces gave targeting help to Ansarallah, known as the Houthis, while avoiding clashes with them. Two sources say the UAE shared intelligence directly for strikes inside Yemen, but not on Saudi soil. Saudi Ambassador Reema Bandar Al-Saud condemned the Houthis as a terrorist threat, while Houthi official Mohammed al-Bukhaiti and UAE-backed groups denied the claims. The unconfirmed report highlights fractures since Saudi forces pushed UAE troops out of Yemen last December.

data.hook: Explosions light up the rugged coastline as Yemeni forces release striking video of ballistic missiles slamming into enemy positions near a vital sea strait.
data.name: Yemen Releases Footage of Missile Strikes on Saudi-Backed Forces in Ras al-Ara
data.summary: On October 5, 2026, Yemeni armed forces shared drone and aerial footage showing locally made ballistic missiles hitting concentrations of Saudi-backed troops and vehicles in Ras al-Ara, a coastal spot in Lahj Governorate. The targeted area sits near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key chokepoint linking the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean, amid renewed clashes with forces loyal to the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council. Yemeni sources called the strikes a response to enemy buildups, with the video capturing burning vehicles, smoke plumes, and precise hits on convoys confirmed by independent observers.

data.hook: Tankers came under fire from unknown projectiles and small boats, but crews stayed safe amid rising tensions in vital shipping lanes.
data.name: Fresh Tanker Attacks Reported in Persian Gulf and off Yemen
data.summary: On October 16, UKMTO reported two attacks northeast of Al Jubayl, Saudi Arabia: one tanker hit by a projectile 68 nautical miles from port with crew evacuated safely, and another damaged by a rocket-propelled grenade from a small boat 78 nautical miles out, with all crew accounted for. The next day, an LNG tanker 140 nautical miles southeast of Al Mukalla, Yemen, faced a skiff with seven people that fired two shots; the ship's security fired warning shots, and the skiff retreated. These incidents, deeper in the Persian Gulf than many before, add to dozens of recent alerts, prompting calls for vigilance as oil and gas routes face disruption risks—though UKMTO has not attributed blame.

data.hook: Yemeni authorities seized shipments of missile components last year, revealing the Houthis' push to craft advanced weapons at home rather than rely on Iran.
data.name: Houthis Build Ballistic Missiles with Chinese Parts, Experts Say
data.summary: Weapons experts from Conflict Armament Research analyzed parts like custom metal pieces, stabilizing fins, and rocket motors linked to Iran's Kheibar Shekan missile, traced to Chinese suppliers. These could enable the Houthis to produce medium-range ballistic missiles reaching up to 1,200 miles, targeting Saudi Arabia and Israel. The Saudi-led coalition called it a dangerous milestone for a terrorist group and urged global efforts to halt such technology transfers amid ongoing Yemen conflict attacks.
